QF.id: SEBI Guidelines for AML Standards, CFT and PF with KYC Norms_9

question.text: Registered intermediaries are required to identify PEPs through which of the following procedures?

answer.text: Procedures that include methods such as seeking relevant information from clients, referring to publicly available information, and accessing commercial electronic PEP databases
Only seeking relevant information from the client
Only referring to publicly available information
Only accessing commercial electronic databases of PEPs

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's AML/CFT guidelines say intermediaries must put in place risk-management procedures to identify whether a client or beneficial owner is a politically exposed person. Such procedures shall include methods such as seeking relevant information from the client, referring to publicly available information, and accessing commercial electronic PEP databases. If an existing client later becomes a PEP, senior-management approval is required to continue the relationship. The Trap: Each "Only..." option states one legitimate identification method, but the guideline expects intermediaries to draw on a combination of these methods rather than relying on any single source. Note: If an existing client subsequently becomes a PEP, the intermediary must obtain senior-management approval to continue the business relationship and apply enhanced due diligence going forward.
